answer: The knoll test I would run is Proof of unique CPA license CPE record: continuing education logged every year for a decade, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. What the farm fears is not one hard check but a check that cannot be shared: continuing education logged every year for a decade is per-account by construction, and the reef is that the tenth clone costs as much as the first. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The kernel grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
